# superset_database_engines (Data Source)

Lists the database engines the Superset instance can connect to: the dialects whose drivers are installed, with the shape of their connection URI, for example to check that a driver is available before creating a `superset_database` connection. Preferred engines come first, then the others by name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "superset_database_engines" "all" {}

# Fail the plan when the instance has no PostgreSQL driver.
data "superset_database_engines" "postgres" {
  engine = "postgresql"
}

check "postgres_driver" {
  assert {
    condition     = length(data.superset_database_engines.postgres.engines) > 0
    error_message = "Superset has no PostgreSQL driver installed."
  }
}

output "engines" {
  value = [for e in data.superset_database_engines.all.engines : "${e.name} (${e.engine})"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `engine` (String) Keep the entries of this SQLAlchemy dialect only, for example `postgresql`.

### Read-Only

- `engines` (Attributes List) The engines. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--engines))

<a id="nestedatt--engines"></a>
### Nested Schema for `engines`

Read-Only:

- `available_drivers` (List of String) Drivers installed for the engine.
- `default_driver` (String) Driver Superset uses when the URI names none; null when the engine has no default.
- `engine` (String) SQLAlchemy dialect, the scheme of the connection URI.
- `name` (String) Name of the engine as the UI shows it, for example `PostgreSQL`.
- `preferred` (Boolean) Whether the UI lists the engine among the preferred ones.
- `sqlalchemy_uri_placeholder` (String) Shape of the connection URI of the engine.
- `supports_file_upload` (Boolean) Whether files can be uploaded into a connection of the engine.
- `supports_ssh_tunneling` (Boolean) Whether a connection of the engine can go through an SSH tunnel.
